scenarios.question: What does Rule 23 of the Trade Marks Rules, 2017 require?
scenarios.answer: An application for trademark registration must be made in Form TM‑A and signed by the applicant or his agent [1]. It must contain a precise description of the mark, a graphical representation, and, where applicable, a statement that the mark is three‑dimensional or consists solely of a colour combination [1].

scenarios.question: What does section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970 exclude from patentability?
scenarios.answer: Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970 excludes from patentability any invention that, in effect, is traditional knowledge or that merely aggregates or duplicates the known properties of traditionally known component(s)[1].

scenarios.question: What is the term of copyright in a literary work published in the lifetime of the author?
scenarios.answer: The copyright in a literary work published during the author's lifetime subsists until sixty years from the beginning of the calendar year next following the year in which the author dies [1].

scenarios.question: Under which provision may a compulsory licence be granted over a registered plant variety?
scenarios.answer: A compulsory licence over a registered plant variety may be granted under Section 47 of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001, as provided for in Rule 71 of the 2003 Rules [1].

scenarios.question: How do the Patents Act and the Patents Rules divide the time limit for requesting examination?
scenarios.answer: The Patents Act requires that a request for examination be made within the “prescribed period” but does not itself set the length of that period [1]. The Patents Rules divide the time limit by specifying a general 48‑month period from the priority date or filing date (whichever is earlier), a similar 48‑month period for requests under sub‑section (3) of section 11B, a period of 48 months or six months after revocation of a secrecy direction (whichever is later) for requests under sub‑section (4), and for applications filed before 1 January 2005 the longer of the statutory period before the 2005 amendment or the period prescribed in the Rules [2].

scenarios.question: Who may apply for registration of a geographical indication, and what must the application contain?
scenarios.answer: Any association of persons or producers or any organisation or authority established by law representing the interest of the producers of the concerned goods may apply in writing to the Registrar for registration of a geographical indication [1]. The application must contain a statement describing how the indication designates the goods as originating from the specified territory with its specific quality, reputation or other characteristics, the class of goods, a map of the territory, details of the appearance of the indication, particulars of the producers to be initially registered, and any other particulars prescribed [1].

scenarios.question: Is the mere discovery of a new form of a known substance patentable in India?
scenarios.answer: No, the mere discovery of a new form of a known substance is not patentable in India because Section 3(d) of the Patents Act expressly states that such a discovery, unless it enhances the known efficacy of the substance, is not an invention within the meaning of the Act [4]. Consequently, a patent granted for such a claim could be revoked on the ground that the subject is not an invention under the Act [3].
